app_info.subtitle: Work your B2B lead pipeline
app_info.description:
Leadbay is a B2B prospecting workspace that sources and scores companies against a seller's ideal customer profile. This app connects ChatGPT to the user's own Leadbay account so they can work that pipeline in plain language instead of clicking through the web app.

Typical sessions: pull the day's fresh, AI-scored prospects and skim the best ones; research a single company in depth (qualification signals, contacts, recent web findings, past notes and activity); draft a personalised outreach email or call opener for a named contact; plan which accounts to visit in a city before a trip; import a list of companies and have Leadbay qualify them; and log what was actually sent so the pipeline stays honest.

It also covers the account admin a seller needs along the way: managing lenses (saved audiences), campaigns, contacts, CRM custom fields, and the qualification questions every lead is scored against.

Lead and contact data is read and written only in the signed-in user's own Leadbay workspace, over an OAuth token the user grants. Three tools are the exception and send nothing else: "send feedback" delivers a message the user wrote to the Leadbay team's Sentry inbox, "report a problem" emits one product-analytics event to PostHog carrying the user's own words, and the interactive-artifact runtime reports its own failures as a bounded error code with no user text in it. The first two fire only when the user asks or accepts an offer, and none of the three carries lead or contact data. The app does not send email or messages on the user's behalf — it drafts outreach and records the outcome the user reports.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads one lead-delivery job with GET /mcp/jobs/{id} and returns its funnel and results so far. It starts nothing and changes nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: The job belongs to the signed-in user's Leadbay organisation and is read from their own workspace. Nothing on the public internet is contacted.
justifications.destructive_justification: A status read. No record is removed or replaced.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. After reading the lens wishlist it posts the returned lead ids to /interactions as LEAD_SEEN, which is what ages those leads out of the user's Discover list.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads the user's own lens and its wishlist inside their Leadbay workspace. No public-web fetch and no third-party provider is involved.
justifications.destructive_justification: The only write is a seen-receipt on leads the user was just shown. Nothing is deleted and no field the user authored is overwritten.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. When the caller passes set_filter the tool first posts it to /monitor/filter, which replaces the filter stored on the user's account before the Monitor view is read.
justifications.open_world_justification: Monitor is the user's own follow-up list inside their Leadbay workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: It replaces one stored filter object that the user can set again at any time; no lead, note or contact is touched.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. It runs the same Monitor read as leadbay_pull_followups, including the optional POST /monitor/filter that replaces the stored filter, and then adds coordinates for mapping.
justifications.open_world_justification: Geo resolution uses Leadbay's own /geo/search index and the leads are the user's own. No public-web call is made.
justifications.destructive_justification: Same single stored filter as the Monitor read. No lead data is removed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. It combines the Monitor read (which may replace the stored filter) with a Discover pull, and the Discover pull reports every returned lead to /interactions as LEAD_SEEN.
justifications.open_world_justification: Both halves read the signed-in user's own leads; city resolution uses Leadbay's own geo index.
justifications.destructive_justification: Writes a seen-receipt and, when a filter is supplied, replaces the stored Monitor filter. It deletes nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: One GET /campaigns with roll-up counters. It creates, updates and deletes nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: Campaigns are rows in the signed-in user's Leadbay organisation.
justifications.destructive_justification: A list read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads GET /campaigns/{id}/leads and derives per-lead progression counters in memory.
justifications.open_world_justification: The campaign and its leads live in the user's own workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: A read of campaign membership; nothing is added or removed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Joins GET /campaigns/{id}/contacts and GET /campaigns/{id}/leads into one call-ready payload. Both are reads.
justifications.open_world_justification: Contacts and leads are records in the user's own Leadbay organisation.
justifications.destructive_justification: No contact or lead is modified; the join happens in memory.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. After assembling the lead profile it posts LEAD_SEEN and LEAD_CLICKED for that lead to /interactions, so Leadbay stops offering it as a new lead.
justifications.open_world_justification: Every sub-resource read (profile, qualification answers, cached web-research summary, contacts, activities) is fetched from the user's own workspace. The cached summary is read, not re-fetched from the web.
justifications.destructive_justification: The interaction receipt is the only write. No note, contact or qualification answer is altered.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. Resolution itself is a query, but the tool then delegates to leadbay_research_lead_by_id, which posts LEAD_SEEN and LEAD_CLICKED for the resolved lead.
justifications.open_world_justification: POST /leads/resolve searches Leadbay's own company registry and the user's own leads. No external search engine is queried.
justifications.destructive_justification: Writes a seen-receipt on the lead it resolved. Nothing is removed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Three GETs: the organisation's AI-agent questions, its ideal buyer profile and its targeting prompt. It is the read-before-write companion to leadbay_set_qualification_questions.
justifications.open_world_justification: All three belong to the signed-in user's organisation.
justifications.destructive_justification: A configuration read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns a static walkthrough script held in the server. It makes no API call at all.
justifications.open_world_justification: No network call leaves the process.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is written anywhere.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. It reads the lead and the org's custom-field catalogue, then posts LEAD_SEEN and LEAD_CLICKED for that lead, matching the behaviour of the other single-lead reads.
justifications.open_world_justification: The lead and the custom-field catalogue are in the user's own workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Only the interaction receipt is written; custom-field values are returned untouched.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. It layers the lead's full notes and activity timeline on top of the research payload, and that research step posts LEAD_SEEN and LEAD_CLICKED.
justifications.open_world_justification: Notes, activities and the research payload are the user's own records.
justifications.destructive_justification: Reads history and writes a seen-receipt. No note or activity is edited or deleted.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. When a filter is supplied it first posts it to /monitor/filter, replacing the stored filter, before scanning cached web-research summaries across the matching leads.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads summaries already stored on the user's leads. It does not trigger a new crawl and contacts nothing outside the workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Replaces the single stored Monitor filter. The leads themselves are read-only here.

justifications.read_only_justification: One GET /kpi/users for the requested look-back window. Non-admin callers are scoped to themselves by the backend.
justifications.open_world_justification: KPI rows describe the user's own Leadbay organisation.
justifications.destructive_justification: A reporting read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. To read the backend's previously-enriched-titles field it selects the lens leads server-side (POST /leads/selection/select), runs an enrichment preview, then clears the selection — so the user's stored selection is replaced.
justifications.open_world_justification: The preview is a price and coverage quote computed inside Leadbay. No contact-data provider is called and nothing is ordered.
justifications.destructive_justification: It overwrites and then clears the transient server-side selection. No contact, lead or enrichment record is deleted.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads /users/me, the organisation's quota status, its lenses and its targeting configuration. Nothing is set.
justifications.open_world_justification: Account and quota state belong to the signed-in user.
justifications.destructive_justification: A status read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads GET /leads/bulk_enrichments/{id}/leads plus each lead's contacts to report progress on a job that was launched earlier.
justifications.open_world_justification: It polls a job inside the user's workspace. The provider call happened in leadbay_enrich_titles, not here.
justifications.destructive_justification: Polling only; it cannot cancel or alter the job.

justifications.read_only_justification: Refreshes qualification answers and cached research for the given leads with GETs only. It never launches a new qualification pass.
justifications.open_world_justification: Both reads are against the user's own leads, and the web-research summary returned is the one already stored.
justifications.destructive_justification: A refresh read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads GET /imports/{id} and its rows for an import the user already started. One pass, no polling loop.
justifications.open_world_justification: The import belongs to the user's organisation.
justifications.destructive_justification: Reports on an import; it cannot re-run or roll one back.

justifications.read_only_justification: POST /leads/resolve is a matcher: it takes candidate rows and answers which existing Leadbay companies they correspond to. No import is created and no row is written.
justifications.open_world_justification: Matching runs against the user's own leads and Leadbay's company registry.
justifications.destructive_justification: Returns matches and a suggested mapping. The user still has to run the import separately.

justifications.read_only_justification: One GET /lenses/{id}/seed_candidates. It exists so the agent can pick seeds before calling leadbay_extend_lens, and it changes nothing by itself.
justifications.open_world_justification: The candidates come from the user's own lens.
justifications.destructive_justification: A read.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. The field catalogue itself is a GET, but when the caller passes sample rows the tool uploads them as a CSV to POST /imports to obtain the backend's mapping hints, which creates an import record.
justifications.open_world_justification: The upload goes to the user's own Leadbay workspace and the sample rows come from the user's own file.
justifications.destructive_justification: It creates a preview import row; it does not modify the org's field definitions or any existing import.

justifications.read_only_justification: One GET of the sector taxonomy in the requested language.
justifications.open_world_justification: The taxonomy is served by the user's own Leadbay region.
justifications.destructive_justification: Reference data, read-only.

justifications.read_only_justification: One GET against Leadbay's /geo/search index to turn a place name into administrative-area ids.
justifications.open_world_justification: The geo index is part of the Leadbay API the user is signed in to. No third-party mapping service is called and no location of the user is requested.
justifications.destructive_justification: A lookup.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. With enrich set to true it orders contact details for the recommended contact and then polls for them; without it, it still marks the lead as seen while assembling the brief.
justifications.open_world_justification: Ordering contact details sends the contact to Leadbay's third-party contact-data providers, which is a call outside the user's workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Enrichment adds email and phone to a contact record. Nothing is deleted, and the brief itself is assembled from reads.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. It delivers a problem report the user asked to send.
justifications.open_world_justification: The report is sent to Leadbay's PostHog project, a third-party service outside the user's workspace. It carries the user's own words and the tool that failed, never lead or contact data.
justifications.destructive_justification: It sends a message. No Leadbay record is changed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. It marks a notification seen on the backend and removes it from later payloads.
justifications.open_world_justification: The notification belongs to the signed-in user.
justifications.destructive_justification: Acknowledging is a flag change the user can live with; the work the notification described is untouched.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns a JavaScript runtime string and a usage guide that are compiled into the server. No API call is made.
justifications.open_world_justification: Nothing leaves the process.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is written.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. It is the diagnostics channel an interactive artifact uses to report its own failures, so it sends data out of the conversation.
justifications.open_world_justification: The event is routed to Leadbay's Sentry and PostHog projects, both third-party services. Only a bounded enum and an error code travel; never user text.
justifications.destructive_justification: It records a diagnostic event. No user record is affected.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. POST /mcp/search starts a discovery job and writes the delivered companies into the user's workspace.
justifications.open_world_justification: The job searches for companies the user does not have yet, which means Leadbay researching the open web on their behalf, and with channels requested it also queries third-party contact-data providers.
justifications.destructive_justification: It adds companies. Existing leads, notes and lenses are untouched, and a paid pass is withheld until the caller passes confirm.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. POST /mcp/qualify starts a batch that resolves and scores the companies the user named and stores the verdicts.
justifications.open_world_justification: Qualification runs Leadbay's AI web research on each company, and the contact pass queries third-party contact-data providers.
justifications.destructive_justification: It writes verdicts and contacts onto companies. It deletes nothing, and a paid pass is withheld until the caller passes confirm.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. It selects the next unqualified leads server-side and launches AI rescoring plus web research on them.
justifications.open_world_justification: The web-research step has Leadbay fetch each company's public web presence.
justifications.destructive_justification: It replaces the transient server-side selection and adds qualification answers. No lead is removed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. It selects leads server-side and launches a bulk contact-enrichment job for the requested job titles.
justifications.open_world_justification: Enrichment is fulfilled by Leadbay's third-party contact-data providers, outside the user's workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: It adds contacts to leads and replaces the transient selection. Nothing existing is deleted.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. It writes the lens filter with POST /lenses/{id}/filter and, on the default lens, creates a draft copy first.
justifications.open_world_justification: Sector and location names are resolved against Leadbay's own taxonomy and geo index.
justifications.destructive_justification: Destructive: the new filter replaces the lens's stored criteria, and the draft path deletes the temporary lens it created if the write fails.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. It writes the organisation's targeting prompt and may answer the clarification Leadbay raises in response.
justifications.open_world_justification: The prompt and the clarification belong to the user's organisation.
justifications.destructive_justification: Destructive: the new text replaces the organisation's previous targeting prompt, and Leadbay regenerates its lead intelligence from it.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. Picking an option posts it to /organizations/{id}/pick_clarification and stores the result as the new targeting prompt.
justifications.open_world_justification: Both calls stay inside the user's organisation.
justifications.destructive_justification: Destructive: the answer replaces the organisation's stored targeting prompt and triggers regeneration.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. It writes a note on the lead and, when an outcome is given, sets the epilogue status and the contact's prospecting status.
justifications.open_world_justification: Notes and statuses are written to the user's own Leadbay records. The tool sends no email or message itself.
justifications.destructive_justification: It appends a note and sets a status. No note is deleted, and logging the same message id twice writes nothing the second time.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. It delivers a message the user wrote to the Leadbay team.
justifications.open_world_justification: Delivery goes to Leadbay's Sentry inbox, a third-party service, and carries only the user's message and their account region.
justifications.destructive_justification: Sending feedback touches no lead, contact, lens or campaign.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. It uploads the user's rows as a CSV, sets the column mappings and commits the import, which creates leads.
justifications.open_world_justification: The upload and the resulting leads stay in the user's own workspace. No external source is queried.
justifications.destructive_justification: It adds leads and fills fields on rows that match existing companies. Existing notes, contacts and lenses are untouched.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. It runs the import above and then starts AI qualification on every imported lead.
justifications.open_world_justification: The qualification step has Leadbay research each imported company's public web presence.
justifications.destructive_justification: It adds leads and qualification answers. Nothing is deleted.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. POST /leads/{id}/contacts creates a person on the lead.
justifications.open_world_justification: The contact is created in the user's own workspace from details the user supplied.
justifications.destructive_justification: It creates a record. Existing contacts on the lead are left alone.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. POST /contacts/{id}/archive removes the person from the lead.
justifications.open_world_justification: The contact belongs to the user's organisation.
justifications.destructive_justification: Destructive: the person stops appearing on the lead for the whole organisation.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. POST /contacts/{id}/pin sets the priority flag on the person.
justifications.open_world_justification: The contact is in the user's own workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: A flag the user can clear again with leadbay_unpin_contact. Nothing is removed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. POST /contacts/{id}/unpin clears the priority flag.
justifications.open_world_justification: Unpinning changes a flag on a person stored in the user's own workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: It clears a flag; the contact and its details stay.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. It edits the person in place through /contacts/{id}/update.
justifications.open_world_justification: The person being edited is a record in the user's own Leadbay organisation; no directory or data provider is consulted.
justifications.destructive_justification: Destructive: fields sent replace what was there, and passing a field as null erases it.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. It orders email and/or phone for one named contact.
justifications.open_world_justification: The order is fulfilled by Leadbay's third-party contact-data providers, outside the user's workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Marked destructive because an identical repeat spends the organisation's enrichment quota a second time and there is no double-launch guard in front of it, so the host should confirm.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. POST /crm/custom_fields adds a field definition to the organisation's CRM.
justifications.open_world_justification: The definition is stored in the user's own organisation.
justifications.destructive_justification: It adds a definition. Existing fields and their values are untouched.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. It renames the field and can change its type and configuration.
justifications.open_world_justification: The field belongs to the user's organisation.
justifications.destructive_justification: Destructive: a type change can make values already stored on leads unreadable in the new shape.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. DELETE /crm/custom_fields/{id} removes the definition.
justifications.open_world_justification: The CRM field catalogue is configuration on the user's own organisation.
justifications.destructive_justification: Destructive: the field's values disappear from every lead that had one. The tool refuses to run without an explicit confirm.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. It writes the organisation's AI-agent questions and its ideal-buyer anti-patterns.
justifications.open_world_justification: Both are configuration on the user's own organisation.
justifications.destructive_justification: Destructive: the question list is written as a whole, so a question left out of the call is removed. Every lead is rescored against the new set.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. POST /leads/{id}/notes writes a note visible to the whole organisation.
justifications.open_world_justification: The note is stored on the user's own lead.
justifications.destructive_justification: It appends. Earlier notes are not edited or removed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. POST /leads/{id}/like records the user's approval, which feeds future batch composition.
justifications.open_world_justification: The signal is stored on the user's own lead.
justifications.destructive_justification: A per-user preference flag. The lead and its data are unchanged.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. It hides the lead from this user and writes the user's reason as a note on the lead.
justifications.open_world_justification: Both writes stay in the user's own workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: The hide is per-user and reversible, and the reason is appended as a new note rather than replacing one.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. It sets the organisation-wide CRM status on the named leads, and optionally the date it was reached.
justifications.open_world_justification: Statuses are stored on the user's own leads.
justifications.destructive_justification: It sets a status field that can be set again to another value. No lead or note is removed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. POST /campaigns creates a named campaign and can seed it with leads.
justifications.open_world_justification: The campaign is created in the user's own organisation.
justifications.destructive_justification: It creates a grouping. The leads themselves are unchanged.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. POST /campaigns/{id}/leads attaches leads to the campaign.
justifications.open_world_justification: Both campaign and leads are the user's own records.
justifications.destructive_justification: It adds membership, and the backend deduplicates so a repeat adds nothing. No lead is modified.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. DELETE /campaigns/{id}/leads detaches the leads.
justifications.open_world_justification: The campaign belongs to the user's organisation.
justifications.destructive_justification: Destructive: the campaign loses those members. The leads themselves survive outside the campaign.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. POST /lenses/{id}/extra_refill queues an additional batch of leads on the lens.
justifications.open_world_justification: The refill is drawn from companies Leadbay already holds for this workspace; no new web search is started.
justifications.destructive_justification: It adds leads to the lens. The lens criteria and existing leads are untouched.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. Besides listing lenses it can switch which one is active, rename or re-describe one, and delete one.
justifications.open_world_justification: Lenses are saved audiences inside the user's own workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Destructive: the delete branch removes a lens permanently, which is why it refuses to run without an explicit confirm.

justifications.read_only_justification: Not read-only. POST /lenses creates a lens and POST /lenses/{id}/filter writes its criteria.
justifications.open_world_justification: Sector and location names are resolved against Leadbay's own taxonomy and geo index; the lens is created in the user's workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: It creates a lens. If writing the criteria fails it deletes only the lens it just created, and it never changes which lens is active.

test_cases.description: Pull the day's fresh, AI-scored prospects — the app's core daily workflow.
test_cases.expected_output: A ranked list of the account's fresh prospects with a fit score, a short why-it-fits rationale, and the recommended contact for each.

test_cases.description: Look a named company up by name and summarise what the account already knows about it. The name is explicit so the case stands alone.
test_cases.user_prompt: Tell me what we know about CEGEDIM.
test_cases.expected_output: A single company card for CEGEDIM: qualification signals and score, contacts with titles, recent web findings, and prior notes or activity if any exist.

test_cases.description: Draft outreach for a named lead. Verifies the app drafts but never sends.
test_cases.user_prompt: Draft me a personalised outreach email for that company.
test_cases.expected_output: An outreach package: the recommended contact, the angle to lead with, and two or three draft variants. Nothing is sent — the user copies or edits the draft themselves.

test_cases.description: Plan in-person visits for a trip to a city, mixing existing accounts with new prospects.
test_cases.user_prompt: I'm visiting Paris next week — which leads should I go and see?
test_cases.expected_output: A city-scoped visit list mixing existing customers, already-qualified leads and fresh prospects, each with a mode badge, a one-line reason to go, and the contact to ask for. If the account holds no known accounts in that city, the app says so rather than padding the list.

test_cases.description: Log outreach the user actually performed. Exercises a write path with the app's verification requirement.
test_cases.user_prompt: I just emailed their VP of Sales — log that against the company.
test_cases.expected_output: Confirmation that the activity was recorded on the lead, carrying the verification reference the user supplied. The app asks for verification rather than logging an unconfirmed send.

negative_test_cases.description: General web or market research is out of scope — the app only works the user's own pipeline.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Research the latest news about Apple stock and summarise analyst reactions.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked. This is open-web market research, not a lookup against the user's Leadbay pipeline.

negative_test_cases.description: The app drafts and logs outreach but never sends mail. A send request must not route here.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Send this email to jane@example.com from my Gmail account.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked. It has no send capability — it prepares drafts and records outreach the user reports having sent.

negative_test_cases.description: Other CRMs are out of scope. Only Leadbay records are readable or writable.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Update my Salesforce opportunity stage for Acme to Closed Won.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked. It can only change records in the user's Leadbay workspace, not in Salesforce.
